title: ERA5 Reanalysis on Single Levels (hourly and monthly, 0.25°)
description: ERA5 is the fifth-generation ECMWF atmospheric reanalysis of the global climate from 1940 to present, produced for the Copernicus Climate Change Service. This catalogue entry covers the single-level (surface and vertically integrated) fields: near-surface temperature and humidity, precipitation, radiation, wind, pressure, cloud cover, evaporation and other variables, distributed hourly on a regular 0.25° grid, with a separate monthly-averaged product and a 10-member ensemble for uncertainty.
purpose: Provides the full atmospheric reanalysis behind ERA5-Land: variables not in ERA5-Land (e.g. boundary-layer height, total cloud cover, 100 m wind, ensemble spread), a longer record from 1940, and the ensemble uncertainty estimate. Useful as consistent climate context over all of Algeria where station records are sparse.

processing: Four-dimensional variational data assimilation (ECMWF IFS) combining a forecast model with observations from across the world; hourly analyses and short-range forecasts. An uncertainty estimate is sampled by an underlying 10-member ensemble at three-hourly intervals, with pre-computed ensemble mean and spread. The CDS product is a regridded subset of the native-resolution ERA5 data.
validation: No single accuracy figure is given on the CDS page; the CDS quality-assurance tab and Hersbach et al. (2020) describe evaluation against observations and earlier reanalyses. The ensemble spread is offered as an uncertainty estimate.
limitations: Precipitation is a model forecast quantity, not an observation; in the Algerian Tell and Atlas it should be checked against gauges or gauge-based products (e.g. CHIRPS, CRU TS).
At 0.25° (about 28 km) the orography of the Tell and Saharan Atlas, Aurès and Hoggar is smoothed; local temperature and rainfall gradients are not resolved (ERA5-Land offers 0.1° for land variables).
ERA5T (most recent ~3 months) is preliminary and may be revised in the final release.

The observing system changes strongly over time (sparse pre-satellite observations before the 1970s), so long-term trends from early decades must be treated with caution; ensemble spread is larger in data-sparse periods.
Hourly global downloads are large; requests are queued and need a CDS account.

algeria_notes: Distinct from the existing ERA5-Land record: use ERA5 single levels for atmospheric variables (cloud, boundary layer, 100 m wind, dewpoint), for the 1940–1949 decade and for ensemble uncertainty; use ERA5-Land for higher-resolution land-surface variables. Over the Sahara, ERA5 is often the only gap-free source, but precipitation there is rare and model-based.
